title: Shortest Path in a Grid with Obstacles Elimination
summary: Given an m x n grid where each cell is either 0 (empty) or 1 (obstacle), determine the minimum number of steps required to move from the upper left corner (0, 0) to the lower right corner (m - 1, n - 1).
statement: Given an m x n grid where each cell is either 0 (empty) or 1 (obstacle), determine the minimum number of steps required to move from the upper left corner (0, 0) to the lower right corner (m - 1, n - 1). You are allowed to eliminate up to k obstacles. If it is not possible to reach the destination under these conditions, return -1.
constraints: grid is a nonempty zero-one matrix whose start and destination are zero.
Move one cell up, down, left, or right and eliminate at most k entered obstacles.
Return the fewest moves from top-left to bottom-right, or -1 when unreachable.
hints: A position alone is not a complete state; remaining eliminations matter.
BFS by distance while retaining the greatest remaining budget seen at each cell.
Enter a neighbor by subtracting its obstacle bit; enqueue only if its remaining budget improves that cell.
An equal-or-smaller budget at the same cell and no shorter distance can never enable a better continuation.
editorial: Breadth-first search guarantees nondecreasing path length. At a cell, a state with more eliminations remaining dominates one reached no earlier with fewer, so store only the greatest remaining budget per cell. This safely prunes the third state dimension. The independent oracle retains every exact row, column, and number-removed state.

tests.explanation: Eliminating the obstacle at row three, column two gives a six-step path.
Every route needs at least two eliminations, so none is allowed.
